source_evidence: With an immediate annuity, you make a single payment to purchase the annuity and typically start receiving income payments within one year of purchase.
answer: Immediate and deferred annuities differ mainly in when income payments begin. With an immediate annuity, you make a single payment and typically begin receiving income within one year. With a deferred annuity, you make a single payment or flexible payments over time, and the money can accumulate before income payments begin. That accumulation period is called the accumulation phase; the period when payments begin is called the payout phase.
